import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a categorical plot to visualize survival probability by passenger class and sex.
# 'survived' column contains 0s and 1s, so the mean directly represents the survival probability.
g = sns.catplot(
    x='pclass',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    data=df,
    kind='bar',
    palette='viridis', # Choose a color palette for better visual distinction
    height=6,          # Height of the plot (in inches)
    aspect=1.2,        # Aspect ratio of the plot
    errorbar='sd'      # Show standard deviation as error bars
)

# Set the overall title for the figure
g.fig.suptitle('Survival Probability on the Titanic by Passenger Class and Sex', y=1.03, fontsize=16)

# Set axis labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Probability")

# Adjust x-tick labels to be more descriptive for passenger classes
g.set_xticklabels(['First Class', 'Second Class', 'Third Class'])

# Set the legend title
g._legend.set_title("Gender")

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a categorical plot to visualize survival probability by passenger class and sex.
# 'survived' column contains 0s and 1s, so the mean directly represents the survival probability.
g = sns.catplot(
    x='pclass',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    data=df,
    kind='bar',
    palette='viridis', # Choose a color palette for better visual distinction
    height=6,          # Height of the plot (in inches)
    aspect=1.2,        # Aspect ratio of the plot
    errorbar='sd'      # Show standard deviation as error bars
)

# Set the overall title for the figure
g.fig.suptitle('Survival Probability on the Titanic by Passenger Class and Sex', y=1.03, fontsize=16)

# Set axis labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Probability")

# Adjust x-tick labels to be more descriptive for passenger classes
g.set_xticklabels(['First Class', 'Second Class', 'Third Class'])

# Set the legend title
g._legend.set_title("Gender")

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
